description: Frozen replay fixture for the 2026-08-25 -> 2026-08-28 DONKI event cluster. Real retrieved records, not synthetic. Demonstrates: observations -> multiple forecast producers -> conflict and uncertainty -> evidence normalization -> verification -> mission risk state -> human authority -> post-event replay.

provenance_boundary.note: DONKI is NOT the official U.S. operational space weather forecast. Aevion retains this source authority label rather than flattening the record into 'trusted data'.

claim_ceiling: Aevion can preserve competing forecasts, their actual model inputs, later observations, provenance, and unresolved attribution without collapsing uncertainty into a false single answer.

refused_claims.claim: Our model predicted the August 28 impact to within three minutes.
refused_claims.reason: Aevion produced no forecast for this event. Separately, the owner-supplied 08:33Z CCMC aggregate figure could not be found in any retrieved record and is contradicted by the live CCMC value of 09:45Z (see contradicted_inputs).

refused_claims.claim: The ~55-minute agreement of WSA-ENLIL run 48261 demonstrates predictive accuracy or superiority.
refused_claims.reason: The 55-minute nominal difference sits inside a published +/-7 hour uncertainty band. A nominal value falling near the observation inside a 14-hour-wide band is not a precision result.

refused_claims.claim: Aevion predicted the event or produced any of these forecasts.
refused_claims.reason: Every forecast row here was produced by a third-party institution and retrieved from NASA CCMC. Aevion's role is preservation, normalization, and verification only.
NASA's own IPS record hedges: the signature 'may be the arrival of' three different CMEs, with a coronal hole high speed stream possibly combined. No unique causal attribution exists in the source.

refused_claims.claim: DONKI is the official U.S. operational space weather forecast.
refused_claims.reason: CCMC explicitly directs operational users to NOAA SWPC and labels DONKI content 'Experimental Research Information'.

contradicted_inputs.note: The string '08:33' does not appear anywhere in the retrieved CME Scoreboard page. The fixture uses the retrieved 09:45Z value. This is the specific figure behind the forbidden 'within three minutes' claim.

WSA_ENLIL.significance: This is the only run in the cluster that took TWO CMEs as explicit model inputs. That fact lives at the model-run level and is invisible in any event-level representation.

WSA_ENLIL.critical_note: featureCode 'SH' = shock front. NASA labels this a Speculative SHOCK analysis. This is NOT a separate CME. It is a second, alternative analysis of the SAME 10:38Z CME as run 48248. Counting 00:32Z and 10:41Z as two independent forecasts would double-count one event and fabricate a 10-hour spread of 'disagreement' that does not exist between producers.

IPS.observation_note: An enhancement in magnetic field components with B_total increasing from 2nT to 13nT (peaking at 2026-08-28T16:11Z). Solar wind speed increased from approximately 250 km/s to 290 km/s from 2026-08-28T03:00Z to 13:35Z. An additional increase in solar wind speed up to 380 km/s and an increase in temperature is observed at 2026-08-28T13:35Z.
IPS.attribution_note_verbatim: This arrival signature is ongoing and may be the arrival of CME: 2026-08-25T10:38Z, CME: 2026-08-25T12:53Z, and/or CME: 2026-08-25T14:53Z. A coronal hole high speed stream arrival may also be combined with this arrival signature.

HSS.note: Coronal hole high speed stream. Logged event time 14:28Z is AFTER the 08:30Z shock, yet the IPS note states an HSS arrival 'may also be combined with this arrival signature'.

edge_types.SOURCE_FLARE: A CME's originating flare. Structural, high confidence.
edge_types.MODEL_INPUT: A CME was an EXPLICIT numerical input to a named model run. This is a machine-readable fact from WSA-ENLIL cmeInputs, not an inference.
edge_types.DIRECT_LINK: A linkage asserted in a DONKI record's own structured linked-events list. Recorded linkage, NOT a causal claim.
edge_types.POSSIBLE_CAUSE: A candidate upstream driver that the source explicitly hedges ('may be', 'and/or'). Recorded ambiguity, deliberately NOT resolved.
edge_types.COINCIDENT_DRIVER: A separate driver that the source says may be combined with the observed signature. Not a cause, not unrelated.
edge_types.OBSERVED_OUTCOME: The later real observation a forecast is scored against.

edges.hedge_verbatim: A coronal hole high speed stream arrival may also be combined with this arrival signature.

edges.note: Reciprocal. The HSS record's own linkedEvents list contains this IPS, so the association is bidirectional in the archive export.

representation_discrepancies.subject: Whether HSS 2026-08-28T14:28:00-HSS-001 belongs to the direct-link set of IPS 2026-08-28T08:30:00-IPS-001

representation_b.name: DONKI HTML detail view
representation_b.verification_limit: The detail page's 'All directly linked activities:' section rendered EMPTY in our text retrieval (the list is populated client-side and was not captured). We therefore could not independently confirm the three-CME list, nor independently confirm the HSS absence. The owner's report is recorded as OWNER_SUPPLIED, not PROVEN. What IS proven from this page is the hedged attribution note quoted verbatim above.

representation_discrepancies.why_preserved: The two representations of the same NASA record disagree about whether the high speed stream belongs in the linked set. Silently picking one would manufacture a certainty the sources do not jointly support. The disagreement is itself evidence about source semantics: 'directly linked' means something different in the detail view than in the archive export. Preserving that is the product.
representation_discrepancies.not_a_criticism: This is not a defect in NASA's data. The hedged 'may be / and/or / may also be combined' language is correct scientific practice for an ongoing, multi-driver arrival signature with an ICME signature quality of 1. The fixture preserves the hedge rather than resolving it.

normalized_forecast_table.sign_convention: signed_error_minutes = predicted_arrival - observed_arrival. POSITIVE = forecast was LATE (predicted after the observation). NEGATIVE = forecast was EARLY.
normalized_forecast_table.ordering: Ranked by predicted arrival time ascending. This is a COMPARISON, not a sequence; row order carries no procedural meaning.

They are not two independent producers disagreeing. Any spread statistic computed over all nine rows inherits this double count.

axes.basis: IPS 2026-08-28T08:30:00-IPS-001 recorded at Earth, detected by 6 instruments across 3 platforms (SOLAR-1, ACE, IMAP). Machine-readable, retrieved from the DONKI archive export.

NASA's own IPS note hedges across three CMEs with 'may be ... and/or', plus a possibly combined coronal hole high speed stream. Two DONKI representations additionally disagree on whether the HSS belongs in the direct-link set. Unresolved in the source; deliberately unresolved here.

Every row carries producer, model identity, analysis type, explicit CME model inputs where exposed, uncertainty band, submission timestamp, and source authority. Four rows carry a machine-readable WSA-ENLIL run ID with its cmeInputs array.
CCMC labels this 'Experimental Research Information' and directs operational users to NOAA SWPC. Aevion retains that boundary rather than flattening it.
Determined by the consuming mission's policy, not by this system. Aevion assembles evidence and applies a policy check; a human holds mission authority.

implemented_policy_state.why: The implemented policy_check() returns UNKNOWN when no model score exists. Aevion produced no forecast for this event, so there is no score. The fixture reports the state the code actually emits rather than inventing decision vocabulary the codebase does not produce.
implemented_policy_state.human_authority_notice: This system does not launch, abort, or authorize anything. It assembles evidence and applies a policy check; a human holds mission authority and makes the decision.
